Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG•NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. West Triangle, Quezon City http: diig.gov.ph OPINION NO. 211 25 MAY ZOIb s. 20].-L MR. IRINEO C. VILLAS Sangguniang Bayan Secretary Municipality of Inocopan Province of Leyte Dear Mr. Villas: This has reference to your letter dated 16 May 2017 requesting for a second Legal Opinion on the following quoted questions: "1. 2. 3. 4. Are appropriations from the 20% Development Fund if not disbursed/implemented for that particular budget year be automatically considered as Continuing Appropriation even if it is not put under Capital Outlay? If considered Continuing Appropriations who will determine or who will declare that said appropriations are continuing? Is it the Local Finance Committee? Is it the Local Chief Executive? Is it the Sangguniang Bayan thru subsequent enactment? If it is not automatically considered as Continuing Appropriations will it be reverted to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund or to the 20% Development Fund? If it is not automatically considered as Continuing Appropriation, will the use of the same in the following year for the purpose stipulated is valid and legal without any subsequent enactment? If it is not valid and legal what is the violation?" Per your letter dated 16 May 2017, the first opinion on the foregoing queries was rendered by the Department and Budget Management (DBM). However, an argument was presented stating that "the cited provisions of R.A. 7160 never mentioned Special Purpose Appropriation or Non Office Expenditures, what is mentioned is capital outlay." Hence, this request for second legal opinion.

Considering that queries number 2 to 4 are deemed sub-questions dependent on the answer for query number I, may we provide a single discussion to address the foregoing concerns. This Department's opinion is in agreement with the opinion rendered by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). DBM Legal Opinion dated 27 March 2017 cited the respective definitions of "Capital Outlays" and "Continuing Appropriations". It clarified that the items of appropriation covered by the 20% development fund have to be presented by expense class. Hence, although not indicated as "Capital Outlay" in the budget documents, it nevertheless fall within the ambit of capital outlays and continuing appropriations. We cannot disagree on this position. Sections 306 (d) and (e) provides for the definitions of Capital Outlays" and "Continuing Appropriations" which respectively read as follows: '(d) "Capital Outlays" refers to appropriations for the purchase of goods and services, the benefits of which extend beyond the fiscal year and which add to the assets of the local government unit concerned, including investments in public utilities such as public markets and slaughterhouses; (e) "Continuing Appropriation" refers to an appropriation available to support obligations for a specified purpose or projects, such as those for the construction of physical structures or for the acquisition of real property or equipment, even when these obligations are incurred beyond the budget year; " Considering that the projects funded by the 20% IRA for development projects involve purchase of goods and services, the benefits of which extend beyond the fiscal year and which add to the assets of the local government unit concerned; and considering further that the 20% IRA for development projects is intended for support obligations or projects, such as those for the construction of physical structures or purchase of equipment; it necessarily follow that the subject budget appropriations fall within the ambit of "Capital Outlays" and "Continuing Appropriations". It was explained by DBM that a subsequent enactment by the Sanggunian is no longer necessary to classify the same as "Continuing Appropriations" since it remains valid until fully spent for the project for which it was appropriated or reverted to the general fund, as the case may be. The same is consistent with the this Department's opinion discussed in DILG Legal Opinion No. 20, s. 2014, which states as follows:

"(F)ollowing Section 322 in relation to Section 323 of the Code, appropriations for contractual obligations of LGUs, such as the infrastructure project funded from the 20% economic development fund that were authorized in the budget of the preceding year as in this case, may be lawfully disbursed until the project is completed. VVhat the law prohibits is the implementation of new projects or the incurring of new obligations under a reenacted budget, as well as the disbursement of funds not authorized in the annual/supplemented budgets for the preceding year. " Notwithstanding the foregoing opinion, may it be clarified that this Department does not have "appellate jurisdiction" over DBM opinions, DBM and DILG being co-equal. We likewise respect the competence of DBM on matters concerning local government finance. Hence, whenever there is still doubt as to the propriety of the opinion herein provided, the concerned party may submit the same to DBM Central Office or to the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) of the Department of Finance for appropriate disposition. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORI F THE SECRETARY AUS A. PANADERO Undersecretary Legal/"
